objective: Identify original construct sources, paper-level operationalizations, independent validity or critique, and statistical forecast methods needed to justify the frozen ASPR v6 innovation-evidence and future-influence prediction registries.
discovery_channels: Backward and forward citation chaining from the ASPR v5 framework bibliography.
Targeted title, construct, formula, and DOI searches in publisher landing pages and scholarly web indexes.
DOI and bibliographic metadata reconciliation against the version-of-record landing page when accessible.
Local review of formula feasibility and time direction against the frozen ASPR source inventory.
query_blocks: (scientific novelty OR recombinational novelty) AND (unusual combinations OR first-time combinations OR cited references) AND (indicator OR validation)
(interdisciplinarity OR knowledge diversity OR cognitive distance) AND (variety OR balance OR disparity OR Rao-Stirling) AND publication
(structural variation analysis OR boundary spanning) AND (modularity change OR cluster linkage OR centrality divergence)
(citation counts OR scholarly impact) AND (determinants OR interpretation OR fixed window OR hurdle model)
(bibliographic coupling OR knowledge network) AND (centrality OR clustering OR citations)
(probabilistic forecast) AND (proper scoring OR calibration OR sharpness OR prediction interval)

source_selection_rules.S1: Prefer the original construct or mathematical-method source over later secondary summaries.
source_selection_rules.S2: Require at least one paper-level scientometric operationalization for every retained innovation dimension.
source_selection_rules.S3: Seek independent construct-validity evidence or a published critique; do not rely only on the indicator authors.
source_selection_rules.S4: Require a DOI or stable version-of-record locator and reconcile title, authors, year, and formula role.
source_selection_rules.S5: Admit only sources whose construct can be separated from future outcomes, exposure controls, scientific quality, and acceptance.
source_selection_rules.S6: Assess whether the cited formula can be reproduced from frozen local data under source_max_year < publication_year; otherwise mark conditional or exploratory.
source_selection_rules.S7: Record adverse or null validation evidence and downgrade roles rather than selecting only favorable findings.
source_selection_rules.S8: Do not treat project-defined thresholds, composites, taxonomies, or approximations as literature-defined; register and validate them separately.

exclusion_rules: Exclude a source as direct publication-time innovation support when its indicator requires forward citations or post-publication reuse.
Exclude non-peer-reviewed reviews as authoritative formula or validity sources; they may only aid discovery.
Exclude studies that only relate a variable to citations when they do not establish that the variable measures innovation.
Exclude unverifiable, incomplete, or semantically mismatched formulas.
Exclude sources requiring unavailable external modalities from the primary local-frozen implementation.
Exclude author, institution, venue-prestige, and attention variables from innovation evidence even if predictive.
limitations: This is a targeted scoping evidence map supporting a prespecified measurement framework, not a PRISMA systematic review or meta-analysis.
Search coverage is strongest for bibliometric, network, and forecast-method literature; domain-specific definitions of scientific originality are outside scope.
Source inclusion establishes conceptual or methodological support, not empirical promotion in ASPR; promotion requires the separate P1-P8 runtime audit.
DOI verification does not establish that an ASPR adaptation is source-equivalent; I9/P5 equivalence testing remains mandatory.

UZZI2013.citation: Uzzi B et al. (2013), Atypical Combinations and Scientific Impact, Science.
UZZI2013.decision_reason: Seminal paper-level cited-source combination operationalization with explicit atypicality and conventionality components.
UZZI2013.limitations: Originally tied to future citation impact and a specific journal-pair null model; the ASPR approximation is conditional until equivalence passes.

LEE2015.citation: Lee Y-N, Walsh JP, Wang J (2015), Creativity in scientific teams: Unpacking novelty and impact, Research Policy.
LEE2015.decision_reason: Defines the U-family lower-tail commonness operationalization later subjected to independent validation.
LEE2015.limitations: OpenAlex source units and the historical comparison corpus differ from the original implementation.

WANG2017.citation: Wang J, Veugelers R, Stephan P (2017), Bias against novelty in science, Research Policy.
WANG2017.decision_reason: Provides the first-time journal-combination family and distance rationale.
WANG2017.limitations: Published variants include reuse/difficulty choices and independent validity is mixed; ASPR therefore keeps the signal profile-only and conditional.

BORNMANN2019.citation: Bornmann L et al. (2019), Do we measure novelty when we analyze unusual combinations of cited references?, Journal of Informetrics.
BORNMANN2019.decision_reason: Independent paper-level validation supports the U family more consistently and questions the first-time W family.
BORNMANN2019.limitations: Validation is biomedical and range-restricted, so cross-domain promotion still requires local tests.

FONTANA2020.citation: Fontana M, Iori M, Montobbio F, Sinatra R (2020), New and atypical combinations: An assessment of novelty and interdisciplinarity, Research Policy.
FONTANA2020.decision_reason: Directly tests and challenges the separation of prevailing novelty indicators from interdisciplinarity.
FONTANA2020.limitations: Its adverse findings do not invalidate every implementation but require explicit discriminant tests and conservative roles.

STIRLING2007.citation: Stirling A (2007), A general framework for analysing diversity in science, technology and society.
STIRLING2007.decision_reason: Foundational decomposition that prevents breadth, balance, and disparity from being treated as interchangeable.
STIRLING2007.limitations: Does not define the exact OpenAlex taxonomy, time window, or ASPR composite weights.

RAFOLS2010.citation: Rafols I, Meyer M (2010), Diversity and network coherence as indicators of interdisciplinarity, Scientometrics.
RAFOLS2010.decision_reason: Paper-level operationalization connects diversity components and integration/coherence while preserving their distinction.
RAFOLS2010.limitations: Interdisciplinarity is supporting context and cannot be equated with novelty.

WANG2015.citation: Wang J, Thijs B, Glanzel W (2015), Interdisciplinarity and Impact: Distinct Effects of Variety, Balance, and Disparity, PLOS ONE.
WANG2015.decision_reason: Empirically demonstrates that the three diversity components have distinct behavior and should remain visible.
WANG2015.limitations: Relations with citation impact do not make the components direct innovation measures.

LEYDESDORFF2019.citation: Leydesdorff L, Wagner CS, Bornmann L (2019), Interdisciplinarity as diversity in citation patterns among journals, Journal of Informetrics.
LEYDESDORFF2019.decision_reason: Supports citation-pattern distance as an operational cognitive-distance structure.
LEYDESDORFF2019.limitations: ASPR field-level, five-year, strictly prior profiles are a frozen implementation choice requiring stability testing.

CHEN2012.citation: Chen C (2012), Predictive effects of structural variation on citation counts, JASIST.
CHEN2012.decision_reason: Original structural variation framework and formula family.
CHEN2012.limitations: Software graph construction and scaling conventions must be matched; generic modularity drop proxies are not equivalent.

SEBASTIAN2021.citation: Sebastian Y, Chen C (2021), The boundary-spanning mechanisms of Nobel Prize winning papers, PLOS ONE.
SEBASTIAN2021.decision_reason: Publishes equations and a known-group application for structural boundary-spanning signals.
SEBASTIAN2021.limitations: Known-group results do not substitute for CiteSpace-equivalence and domain/era stability in ASPR.

ARTS2025.citation: Arts S, Melluso N, Veugelers R (2025), Beyond Citations: Measuring Novel Scientific Ideas and their Impact in Publication Text.
ARTS2025.decision_reason: Supports text-based novelty as a conceptually distinct family from citation-reference recombination.
ARTS2025.limitations: The current frozen ASPR corpus lacks sufficient audited abstract coverage and a locked local model, so the family remains exploratory and unused.

SHI2023.citation: Shi F, Evans J (2023), Surprising combinations of research contents and contexts are related to impact, Nature Communications.
SHI2023.decision_reason: Provides a second text/content operational family and highlights content-context distinctions.
SHI2023.limitations: Requires a frozen text representation and human construct validation unavailable in the current local release.

BORNMANN_DANIEL2008.citation: Bornmann L, Daniel H-D (2008), What do citation counts measure? A review of studies on citing behavior, Journal of Documentation.
BORNMANN_DANIEL2008.decision_reason: Authoritative synthesis supporting citations as multifactorial scholarly-use signals rather than quality truth.
BORNMANN_DANIEL2008.limitations: The review cannot validate ASPR's exact target composite or causal interpretation.

TAHAMTAN_BORNMANN2020.citation: Tahamtan I, Bornmann L (2020), What do citation counts measure? An updated review, Scientometrics.
TAHAMTAN_BORNMANN2020.decision_reason: Updates the evidence base for non-innovation determinants of citation counts and motivates strong controls.
TAHAMTAN_BORNMANN2020.limitations: Determinants vary by corpus, field, and window; local OOF baseline comparisons remain necessary.

MULLAHY1986.citation: Mullahy J (1986), Specification and testing of some modified count data models, Journal of Econometrics.
MULLAHY1986.decision_reason: Methodological basis for separating zero versus positive uptake from positive-outcome magnitude.
MULLAHY1986.limitations: Does not imply that every zero-generating mechanism is identical or that the conditional outcome must follow a specific distribution.

BISCARO2014.citation: Biscaro C, Giupponi C (2014), Co-Authorship and Bibliographic Coupling Network Effects on Citations, PLOS ONE.
BISCARO2014.decision_reason: Paper-level temporal bibliographic-coupling measures directly support a separate opportunity predictor block.
BISCARO2014.limitations: Single thematic corpus and association with citations do not make network position an innovation construct.

GUAN2017.citation: Guan J, Yan Y, Zhang JJ (2017), The impact of collaboration and knowledge networks on citations, Journal of Informetrics.
GUAN2017.decision_reason: Independent evidence that knowledge-network position belongs in citation prediction rather than the innovation profile.
GUAN2017.limitations: Observed associations are corpus-dependent and potentially nonlinear.

GNEITING_RAFTERY2007.citation: Gneiting T, Raftery AE (2007), Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation, JASA.
GNEITING_RAFTERY2007.decision_reason: Provides the formal basis for evaluating uptake probabilities with proper scores rather than rank association alone.
GNEITING_RAFTERY2007.limitations: Does not choose ASPR's model family or performance threshold.

GNEITING_BALABDAOUI_RAFTERY2007.citation: Gneiting T, Balabdaoui F, Raftery AE (2007), Probabilistic forecasts, calibration and sharpness, JRSS B.
GNEITING_BALABDAOUI_RAFTERY2007.decision_reason: Supports joint reporting of calibration and sharpness/coverage for probabilistic forecasts.
GNEITING_BALABDAOUI_RAFTERY2007.limitations: Finite-sample diagnostics still require preregistered implementation and uncertainty intervals.

EXCLUDE_FUNK2017.citation: Funk RJ, Owen-Smith J (2017), A Dynamic Network Measure of Technological Change, Management Science.
EXCLUDE_FUNK2017.decision_reason: Excluded from publication-time innovation evidence because the disruption/consolidation measure is defined by later attention to the focal work and its predecessors.
EXCLUDE_FUNK2017.limitations: May be useful as a separately registered future outcome, but it cannot be a T0 predictor or innovation-profile metric.

EXCLUDE_WU2019.citation: Wu L, Wang D, Evans JA (2019), Large teams develop and small teams disrupt science and technology, Nature.
EXCLUDE_WU2019.decision_reason: Uses post-publication citation behavior and team characteristics; neither can serve as direct publication-time innovation evidence in ASPR v6.
EXCLUDE_WU2019.limitations: Could inform secondary descriptive research but is outside the registered local-frozen outcome set.

EXCLUDE_NOVELTY_REVIEW_PREPRINT2025.citation: Liu X et al. (2025), A review on the novelty measurements of academic papers, arXiv.
EXCLUDE_NOVELTY_REVIEW_PREPRINT2025.decision_reason: Used only to identify candidate families; excluded as authoritative support because a peer-reviewed version and stable final formulas were not established in this evidence map.
EXCLUDE_NOVELTY_REVIEW_PREPRINT2025.limitations: Exclusion is about evidentiary role, not a judgment that the review is uninformative.
